facts.text: Mound City earned its name from a Native American mound where guests at General Rawlings' hotel would sleep to enjoy cool breezes and fewer mosquitoes.
Mound City was incorporated in 1857, merging the town founded by Major General Moses Marshal Rawlings with Emporium City, a Cincinnati‑Cairo development.
In 1862 the Navy moved its Mississippi River Squadron shipyard to Mound City, building a foundry, barracks, and hospital amid frequent floods.
Mound City sits along the Ohio River just north of its confluence with the Mississippi, placing it at a historic river junction.
Mound City serves as the county seat of Pulaski County, Illinois, anchoring the region’s administrative functions.
